clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Whole-exome sequencing of the index patient identified the TNFAIP3 nonsense mutation c.A271T: p.(Lys91*), confirmed using PCR and capillary electrophoresis; family with autosomal-dominant inheritance pattern
Obligate carrier of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation (pedigree inference; mother of the index patient); autoimmune thyroiditis diagnosed at an early age
Familial mutation screening (PCR and capillary electrophoresis) showed the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation; described as an affected family member with autoimmune thyroiditis diagnosed at an early age
Familial mutation screening (PCR and capillary electrophoresis) showed the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation; daughter of the index patient

parental_testing_statement.value: Mutation screened in other family members; the mother (I-2) is described as an obligate carrier (she died of liver failure at 46 years)

functional_evidence_statement.value: 3D modelling (PDB 5LRX) yields a severely truncated protein lacking the complete OTU domain; in HEK293/Flp-In 293 T-REx cells only an N-terminal fragment is expressed (detected only with an N-terminal tag); the p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to suppress TNF-alpha-induced NF-kB activation in a luciferase reporter assay; AP-MS and BioID showed complete loss of interactions with e.g. BRCC3, TRAF2, BIRC2, HUWE1, USP9X, TNIP1, TBK1, CYLD and many weakened interactions; PBMCs of patients II-1 and III-1 showed elevated IL-1beta and IL-18 secretion (canonical and alternative NLRP3 inflammasome activation), increased TNF-alpha secretion, and IL-1beta/IL-18 secretion suppressed by caspase-8 inhibitor Z-IETD-FMK but not by necrostatin-1

pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors.value: predicted to be pathogenic according to the ACMG Standards and Guidelines; loss-of-function mutation
